name: Black Feather Quill
summary: In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Black Feather Quill is needed to wake the Druids of the Talon.

sections.title: A Vessel of Wakening
sections.body: The Black Feather Quill is one of four sacred focuses that wake the Druids of the Talon from hibernation. The others are the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. Together, the focuses call slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Without them, a druid may remain trapped in the Dream, unable to return to their waking body.

sections.title: The Threat in Ban'ethil
sections.body: Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Ban'ethil Barrow Den and threatened the chests that held the relics. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar ordered their swift recovery. The captive druids had to be freed before they were lost to the Dream.

faq.q: What is the Black Feather Quill used for?
faq.answer: The Black Feather Quill is one of four sacred focuses used to wake the Druids of the Talon from hibernation in the Emerald Dream.

faq.q: Where is the Black Feather Quill kept?
aliases: where is chest of black feather
faq.answer: The Black Feather Quill is kept in the Chest of the Black Feather, deep inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den in central Teldrassil.

faq.q: Why can't the druids wake up without the quill and other relics?
aliases: why do druids need relics to wake
can druids wake up on their own
faq.answer: Druidic hibernation sends the druids into the Emerald Dream under delicate enchantments. Without the sacred focuses, their slumbering spirits cannot find their way back to their bodies.

faq.q: Who asks for the Black Feather Quill?
faq.answer: Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar directs adventurers to recover the Black Feather Quill and the other sacred focuses to rescue the imperiled druids.

angles.text: As a druid, you know the quill as one of the sacred tools that tether the Druids of the Talon to the waking world while their spirits commune with the Emerald Dream.
As a night elf, you know the defilement of Ban'ethil's relic chests by Gnarlpine furbolgs as another painful reminder of Teldrassil's encroaching corruption.
